source.name: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open on Escape, and a default dialog must still close
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/43070) at 2bb544eb426e9b1e019c2a98798e0002b8a41d35, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

journey.title: Escape must not dismiss a dialog opened with keyboard: false
journey.goal: The confirmation dialog stays open however often Escape is pressed, so the user can still enter the code and send the transfer

functionalJourney.title: Confirm with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking the backdrop does not close the dialog; entering the code and clicking Send completes the transfer

guards.title: Cancel transfer still closes the dialog from the keyboard
guards.goal: Tabbing to Cancel transfer and pressing Enter closes the dialog and records the cancellation

guards.title: Escape still closes a dialog with the default options
guards.goal: An ordinary dialog created without options opens with Enter and closes with Escape

plan.root_cause: The confirm dialog is created with `keyboard: false` and `backdrop: 'static'`. The native `<dialog>` element fires a `cancel` event on each Escape press. The `_cancelHandler` in `dialog-base.ts` prevents the first two `cancel` events, but the third `cancel` event becomes non-cancelable (observed `cancelable: false`), so `preventDefault()` has no effect and the dialog closes. The existing keydown listener only handles Escape for non-modal dialogs, leaving modal dialogs with `keyboard: false` solely dependent on the `cancel` event handler, which fails on the third press.
plan.repair_strategy: Extend the existing keydown listener in `_addDialogListeners` to also intercept Escape on modal dialogs when `keyboard: false`. By calling `event.preventDefault()` and `event.stopImmediatePropagation()` on the keydown event, we prevent the native `cancel` event from firing in the first place, ensuring the dialog never closes via Escape.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: The confirm dialog (keyboard: false) will no longer close on any number of Escape presses, satisfying the requirement that Escape must not dismiss it. The help dialog (keyboard: true) continues to close on Escape as expected. Focus management and screen-reader behavior remain unchanged.
functional_risks: If the native dialog's cancel event is fired independently of the keydown event (e.g., by a browser-internal mechanism), the keydown interception may not prevent the cancel event. However, the observed behavior suggests the cancel event is triggered by the keydown event, so stopping propagation should work.

The change adds a new code path for modal dialogs with keyboard: false; it must not affect modal dialogs with keyboard: true (they return early) or non-modal dialogs (they continue to work as before).
verification_requirements: Run the provided journey: the confirm dialog must remain open after three Escape presses (attribute 'open' present).
Run the regression guard for the help dialog: Escape must still close the help dialog.
Verify that the cancel button and backdrop clicks still work as expected.
